I remember hearing that BERT was trained on a large dataset of English text and that it's a bidirectional model, which means it processes text from both directions.

Next, the Attention is All You Need (AAUN) architecture, proposed by Vaswani et al., is the original transformer architecture. I believe this model has 8 layers. The key difference between BERT and AAUN is that BERT uses a different number of layers, which allows it to capture more context, making it good for tasks like text generation and question answering.

So, to find out how many more layers BERT has compared to AAUN, I subtract 8 from 12, which gives me 4. That means BERT base has 4 more layers than the AAUN encoder.
